key_insight: This paper introduces an occlusion-robust tracking framework that keeps targets linked to their identities even when they disappear for long periods. The main idea is to prevent trajectory loss during full or long-term occlusion, improving continuity and reliability in real-time tracking.
problem_solved: It addresses the failure of conventional multi-object trackers when a target becomes fully hidden or absent from view, which often causes premature track termination and identity switches. This is especially important in defense and surveillance scenarios where losing a target can reduce situational awareness.
method: Integrates an occlusion-aware tracking strategy designed to preserve target identity across disappearance and reappearance events.
Maintains trajectory continuity instead of ending tracks as soon as detections vanish.
Supports real-time multi-object tracking under full and long-term occlusion conditions.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this improves tracker robustness in hard real-world environments where visibility is intermittent. It can reduce identity loss, improve downstream analytics, and make tracking systems more dependable in safety-critical applications.

paper_title: Tracking the Unseen: An Occlusion-Robust Framework for Target Tracking Under Full and Long-Term Occlusion
paper_authors: Mais Mohammed, Sharifa Mohammed, Hanan Awadh, Haneen Bamaas, Raghad Bawazeer
